summary.headline: The Library Board of Trustees voted to spend up to $1,500 from State Aid funds to repair and reseed a removed asphalt path.
summary.summary: The Library Board of Trustees met to discuss Community Preservation Committee signage requirements for previous grant projects, including the facade and historical archives. The board approved up to $1,500 in State Aid to hire a landscaper to level and reseed a former asphalt pathway. Trustees also reviewed annual budget performance following Town Meeting approval, coordinated logistics for the upcoming Candidates Night and staff appreciation week, and discussed updating the format for the library director annual evaluation.

topics.title: Community Preservation Committee signage for completed projects
topics.summary: A representative from the Community Preservation Committee met with the trustees to discuss installing required signs acknowledging Community Preservation Act funding for completed library projects. The projects include the building facade restoration and the historical collection archiving project.
key_details: Signage is funded through leftover balances in the original Community Preservation Act project articles.
The facade sign will match existing exterior signage produced by Crown Trophy.
A small interior plaque or sign will be placed in the library reference area near the historical collection and historic drugstore sign.
The library director will obtain draft proofs from Crown Trophy for trustee review at the May meeting before sending them to the CPC.
topics.outcome: The director will obtain sign design proofs to present at the May 11 trustee meeting.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: Trustees reviewed and approved the minutes from the March 9, 2026 meeting with minor corrections and later adjourned the meeting.
key_details: Minutes from March 9 were approved with amendments clarifying the salary budget report and inserting a missing word in the Candidates Night section.
The meeting adjourned at 12:21 PM.

topics.title: Director report, budget review and facility updates
topics.summary: The library director reported on the resolution of an accounting discrepancy in the salary budget and updated the board on recent maintenance and upcoming professional events. The town accountant identified that an unbudgeted wage adjustment from fall town meeting had skewed projections, but sufficient salary funds remain for the fiscal year.
key_details: The salary line had approximately $7,000 more available than previously estimated following an adjustment from the fall town meeting.
The Department of Public Works patched potholes in the library parking lot and removed brush from the StoryWalk area.
Custom Alarm plans to install replacement security cameras using State Aid funds after a revised contract agreement was reached.
The library fiscal year 2027 budget passed without debate at Annual Town Meeting.
Three staff members will attend the Massachusetts Library Association conference in Danvers in May, including one staff member presenting a panel on teen volunteering.

topics.title: Asphalt pathway refill and reseeding
topics.summary: Trustees discussed landscaping work needed to fill in and reseed the lawn where an old asphalt path was previously removed. Rather than paying the Department of Public Works for materials, the library solicited a proposal from Curtis Landscaping.
key_details: Curtis Landscaping quoted $1,190 to remove remaining asphalt pieces, fill the trench, and reseed the lawn.
The project will be funded through the library State Aid account.
Trustees authorized spending up to $1,500 to cover the quote and any minor unexpected costs.
topics.outcome: Trustees voted 5-0 to approve spending up to $1,500 from State Aid funds for Curtis Landscaping to reseed and refill the walkway.

topics.title: Emergency disaster plan progress
topics.summary: The director provided an update on drafting an emergency and disaster operations plan for the library building and staff. The Senior Center has been designated as the emergency regrouping location for weekend and evening staff.
key_details: Staff and a community volunteer have completed preliminary editorial reviews of the draft plan.
The facilities department provided a permanent keypad code for library staff to enter the Senior Center in an emergency.
The director aims to finalize the emergency plan before summer.
topics.outcome: Draft plan will be completed ahead of the summer.

topics.title: Library director annual evaluation procedure
topics.summary: The board discussed the evaluation process for the library director under his first year as a contract employee. Trustees agreed to move away from rigid numerical scoring in favor of qualitative questions focusing on successes, items to discontinue, and new goals.
key_details: The director submitted a three-page self-evaluation.
The board chair will distribute a simplified draft evaluation format to trustees.
Trustees were asked to email their evaluation feedback to the board chair by mid-May.
topics.outcome: The chair will email a questionnaire form, and trustees will submit responses by mid-May to compile a composite draft.

topics.title: Candidates Night planning
topics.summary: Trustees reviewed preparations for Candidates Night, an event hosted at the library featuring candidates for the Select Board. The event will begin with a 6:30 PM gathering followed by the formal forum at 7:00 PM, recorded by Southborough Access Media.
key_details: Event flyer is prepared and promotional marketing will begin immediately.
The director will contact Roche Bros. to request a food donation after Wegmans declined.
Trustees agreed to purchase a sandwich platter from Wegmans if donations cannot be secured.
topics.outcome: The director will contact local businesses for refreshment donations.

topics.title: Staff appreciation week and Friends of the Library fundraising
topics.summary: Trustees scheduled daily food and snack coverage for National Library Week staff appreciation and received an update on Friends of the Library fundraising initiatives. The Friends are introducing branded stationery note cards and preparing raffle baskets for the upcoming book sale.
key_details: Trustees divided up coverage to bring food for staff each day Tuesday through Friday.
The Friends purchased 500 blank note cards featuring the library logo in five colors to sell in packs of five for $20.
The note cards will also be used to send acknowledgment notes when donations are made in someone's honor.
Two raffle baskets are being assembled for a drawing during the May book sale.
topics.outcome: Branded cards will arrive by April 23 and raffle tickets will go on sale in May.

topics.title: Book drop concrete platform safety concerns
topics.summary: The director alerted the board to significant winter cracking, settling, and erosion on the exterior concrete pad outside the secondary book drop. Staff have tripped on the cracked slab, prompting discussions about replacing it with an ADA-accessible ramp.
key_details: The concrete landing pad is severely indented and cracked rather than just chipped.
The director will consult the town facilities department and Asphalt Engineering to evaluate repair versus full replacement.
Trustees recommended investigating whether the replacement should include an ADA-compliant ramp.
topics.outcome: The director will seek an assessment and cost estimates from facilities and contractors.

votes.motion: Approve spending up to $1,500 from State Aid funds to hire Curtis Landscaping to reseed and refill the removed asphalt walk area
